findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the memo cache lifecycle: its scope (recommend per-agent-call, created fresh when the wrapper is armed and discarded when the call completes), and confirm no cross-call reuse.
evidence: The wrapper caches allowlisted results: 'first repeat of a signature returns the cached result'
No statement of cache scope, ownership, eviction, or retirement in Approach or Scope
The seam 'arms every tool-bearing Agent call' — implies the cache must be scoped to a single agent invocation, but this is never stated
findings.finding: The plan introduces a memoization cache (shared/mutable state keyed by tool-call signature) but does not define its lifecycle: scope (per-agent-call vs per-process), who creates it and when, whether it accumulates unbounded across a long run, and whether/how it is retired or reset between agent calls.
findings.location: Approach — 'Add a memoize+nudge toolset wrapper at the shared agent-call seam'
scenarios: A long-lived process reuses the wrapper across multiple independent agent calls and serves a stale cached result from a prior task
Cache grows without bound across a very long run
findings.suggested_fix: State that the memo cache is instantiated per agent-call invocation at the seam (same lifetime as the runaway guard's window state), is not shared across independent Agent calls, and is discarded when the call returns.

findings.checklist_item: State that the memo cache and per-signature nudge counter are scoped per Agent call (mirroring the runaway guard's closure-local signatures list), so results and escalation state never leak across separate build_agent_kwargs invocations.
evidence: Guard precedent is per-call closure state: '_runaway_guard_toolsets' builds 'signatures: list[str] = []' and 'checked_steps: set[int]' fresh inside the function invoked per build_agent_kwargs call (agent_call.py:84-85)
Plan says 'memoize+nudge toolset wrapper at the shared agent-call seam' but never fixes whether the cache is per-Agent-call or longer-lived
ABSENCE: no AC or Approach sentence pins cache lifetime; a cross-call cache would key stale read_file/list_directory output to a signature and return it in a later Agent call
findings.finding: The plan does not state the SCOPE/LIFETIME of the memo cache (and the per-signature repeat counter driving nudge escalation). The runaway guard it wraps uses a closure-local signatures list scoped to a single build_agent_kwargs / Agent call; the memo should explicitly share that per-call scope so a cached read result / repeat-count is not reused across separate Agent calls within a gate session.
scenarios: Two separate verifier Agent calls in one session issue the same read_file signature; a process-lifetime cache returns the first call's content in the second
Nudge escalation counter carrying across Agent calls would emit a level-2 nudge on the first repeat of a fresh run
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Approach: 'The memo cache and its per-signature repeat counter are closure-local to each build_agent_kwargs call — the same per-Agent-call scope as the runaway guard's signature list — so nothing is memoized or escalated across separate Agent calls.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Qualify the 'no harness memoizes + steers' novelty claim (Context section) by acknowledging the existing memoize-and-nudge / cached-idempotent-read prior art (e.g. onceonly.tech, production-agent-pattern write-ups) and framing the contribution as its integration at the shared agent_call.py wrapper seam alongside the existing distinct-ratio actuator.
evidence: Plan claim: 'Research across agent harnesses (OpenHands StuckDetector, smolagents max_steps) found detect-and-terminate everywhere but no harness that memoizes the duplicate and steers the model back on course'

Retrieved source onceonly.tech/blog/how-to-stop-ai-agents-repeating-actions: 'Result cache (retry returns the same output). Retry-aware responses (tell the agent "duplicate: true" to stop loops)... You short-circuit and return your cached result... instead of executing again.'

Retrieved source kondasamy.com/blog/2026/15-patterns-production-ai-agents: 'Return cached result]. For read-only tools: they're already idempotent... retries return the cached result instead of re-executing side effects.'

The design is a well-trodden idempotent-read-cache + retry-nudge pattern applied to the pre-existing WrapperToolset seam (agent_call.py _steering_toolsets/_runaway_guard_toolsets), not a novel architecture.
findings.finding: The plan's prior-art survey asserts 'no harness that memoizes the duplicate and steers the model back on course,' but retrievable current sources describe exactly this memoize-and-nudge combination as an existing pattern, so the novelty claim is overstated.
findings.location: Context / Problem section, sentence: 'found detect-and-terminate everywhere but no harness that memoizes the duplicate and steers the model back on course — graduated nudge-then-abort is the recommended pattern.'
scenarios: A reviewer or future author reads the novelty claim as a bright-line justification for a bespoke design and skips evaluating the established cached-idempotent-read + duplicate-nudge pattern.
The 'recommended pattern' phrasing implies a survey conclusion that the retrievable sources actually already document.
